en.title: Documentary Stuns Hollywood, Out-earning New DC Blockbuster in Second Weekend
en.summary: In a box office upset, a three-hour documentary has captured audiences' attention, earning nearly as much as a major comic-book adaptation in its sophomore weekend. This unexpected performance highlights a growing appetite for unconventional narratives among moviegoers.
en.body:
This past weekend, the film industry witnessed a fascinating box office dynamic, with A24's expansive documentary **You Can See Everything** staging a remarkable performance, pulling in an impressive $19.5 million in its second weekend. This figure nearly matched the debut weekend earnings of Warner Bros. and DC's highly anticipated R-rated origin story, **Clayface**, which opened at No. 1 with $24 million. The documentary, a deep dive into the life and times surrounding Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos, defied typical box office trajectories by expanding its release to 2,655 venues and seeing its audience grow.

**Clayface**’s $24 million debut, while strong, was perhaps not the runaway success some might have predicted for a DC villain origin story. The film, described as an R-rated body horror exploration of Matt Hagen's descent into villainy, faced a crowded marketplace. Despite its budget and the established DC brand, it couldn't entirely overshadow the staying power of **You Can See Everything**. The documentary's success is particularly noteworthy given its three-hour runtime and unconventional subject matter, demonstrating a significant audience demand for its unique narrative approach. The film's 10-day total is already approaching $45 million, a testament to its exceptional hold and audience engagement.

## A Documentary's Unlikely Triumph

The sheer tenacity of **You Can See Everything** at the box office is a story in itself. Expanding from its initial limited release, the film resonated with audiences looking for something beyond the typical blockbuster fare. Its ability to hold strong and even increase its earnings in its second weekend, while also expanding its theatrical footprint, is a rare feat, especially when competing against a major studio release like **Clayface**. This success challenges the notion that only conventional genre films can capture widespread audience attention, suggesting that a compelling, well-crafted documentary can indeed become a box office contender.

## What This Means for the Market

For cinephiles and casual moviegoers alike, the performance of **You Can See Everything** offers a refreshing narrative. It underscores the power of word-of-mouth and the potential for A24, a studio known for its distinctive and often challenging film selections, to break through. This win signals that audiences are open to diverse cinematic experiences, and that a film's narrative depth and critical buzz can be as powerful, if not more so, than its franchise pedigree. The film's strong hold also highlights the audience's capacity for engaging with longer, more complex stories, a trend that could influence future programming decisions across the industry.

## What's Next

While **Clayface** has firmly planted itself at the top of the box office charts for its opening weekend, all eyes will be on the sustained performance of **You Can See Everything** in the coming weeks. The continued success of the documentary will be crucial in determining its ultimate box office impact and its place in the annals of breakout documentary hits.
